statement.p: Compute the surface integral over the given oriented surface:

static.solution:
\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = 0, so \iiint_V \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} \, dV=0 where we integrate over the volume enclosed by the region and the xy-plane. By the divergence theorem, the desired integral is then -\iint_{x^2+y^2\leq 9} \mathbf{F}\cdot \mathbf{n}\, dxdy where we integrate over the disk comprising the bottom of the hemisphere. The disk lies in the plane z=0, so \mathbf{n}=\lt 0,0,-1> and the desired quantity becomes \begin{aligned} -\iint_{x^2+y^2\leq 9} \left\lt 0,2,x^2\right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,-1\right> \, dxdy \amp = -\iint_{x^2+y^2\leq 9} -x^2\, dxdy \\ \amp = \int_{-3}^3 \int_{-\sqrt{9-y^2}}^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} x^2\, dxdy \\ \amp = \int_{-3}^3 \left. \frac{x^3}{3} \right\vert_{-\sqrt{9-y^2}}^{\sqrt{9-y^2}} \, dy \\ \amp = \frac{2}{3} \int_{-3}^3 (9-y^2)^{3/2} \, dy \\ \amp = \frac{2}{3} \left. \frac{x(49-2x^2)\sqrt{9-x^2}+3\cdot 9^2 \arcsin(x/3)}{8} \right|_{-3}^3 \\ \amp = \frac{81\pi}{4} \\ \amp = \frac{81\pi }{4} \end{aligned}
The second approach is to attack the integral directly.
We parametrize the hemisphere S by: \mathrm{\Phi }( \theta ,\phi )=( 3 \cos\theta \sin\phi ,3 \sin\theta \sin\phi ,3 \cos\phi),\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi , \,0\le \phi \le \frac{\pi }{2} Step 1. Compute the normal vector.
The normal vector that points to the outside of the hemisphere is: \mathbf{n} ={\mathbf{T} }_{\phi }\times {\mathbf{T} }_{\theta }= 9 \sin\phi \left\lt \cos\theta \sin\phi , \sin\theta \sin\phi , \cos\phi \right> For 0\le \phi \le \frac{\pi }{2} we have \sin\phi \cos\phi \ge 0, therefore \mathbf{n} points to the outside of the hemisphere.
Step 2. Evaluate the dot product \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n}.
We express the vector field in terms of the parameters: \mathbf{F} \left(\mathrm{\Phi }( \theta ,\phi )\right)= \left\lt 0,7,x^2\right> = \left\lt 0,7,9 \,\cos^2\theta \,\sin^2\phi \right> Hence: \mathbf{F} \left(\mathrm{\Phi}(\theta,\phi)\right)\cdot \mathbf{n} (\theta,\phi) =\left\lt 0,7,9 \cos^2\theta \sin^2\phi\right> \cdot 9 \sin\phi \left\lt \cos\theta \sin\phi , \sin\theta \sin\phi , \cos\phi \right>= 9 \sin\phi \left(7\sin\theta\sin\phi + 9 \,\cos^2\theta \,{\sin}^2\phi \cos\phi \right)= 63\sin\theta \,\sin^2\phi +81 \,\cos^2\theta \,\sin^3\phi \cos\phi Step 3. Evaluate the surface integral.
The surface integral is equal to the following double integral: \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iint_{\mathcal{D}} \mathbf{F} \left(\mathrm{\Phi }( \theta ,\phi )\right)\cdot \mathbf{n} ( \theta ,\phi ) \,d\theta\, d\phi= \int_0^{\pi/2} \int_0^{2\pi } \left(63\sin\theta\sin^2\phi +81 \,\cos^2\theta \sin^3\phi \cos\phi \right) \,d\theta \, d\phi= \int_0^{\pi/2} \int_0^{2\pi } 63 \sin\theta \sin^2\phi \,d\theta\, d\phi +\int_0^{\pi/2} \int_0^{2\pi } 81 \,\cos^2\theta \,\sin^3\phi \cos\phi \,d\theta \, d\phi= \left(\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^2\phi \,d\phi \right)\left(\int_0^{2\pi } 63 \sin\theta \,d\theta \right) +\left(\int_0^{\pi/2} 81 \,\sin^3\phi \cos\phi \,d\phi \right)\left(\int_0^{2\pi } \cos^2\theta \,d\theta \right)= \left(\left.\frac{\phi }{2}-\frac{\sin 2\phi }{4}\right|_{\phi = 0}^{\pi/2}\right)\left(-63 \cos\theta \bigg|_{\theta =0}^{2\pi }\right) +\left(\left.\frac{81 \,\sin^4\phi }{4}\right|_{\phi = 0}^{\pi/2}\right)\left(\left.\frac{\theta }{2}+\frac{\sin 2\theta }{4}\right|_{\theta =0}^{2\pi }\right)= 0+\frac{81}4\cdot \pi =\frac{81\pi }{4}
